WHEN orch lesson add has no --scope, or a scope other than local or basicly, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse it by name and append no event.
WHEN orch lesson add has --scope basicly, THE COMMAND SHALL require the failing check and a reproduction command, and SHALL record the installed basicly version itself.
WHEN any lesson text matches MACHINE_PATH_RULES, ABSOLUTE_PATH_RULE or the machine-username rule, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse it, name the rule, and append no event.

The record and the command help state that host names are not detected.
Tests in tests/ cover each refusal and one accepted lesson of each scope.
payload.description:
## Context
Cut L1b of the shape of basicly-1dpggot (Orchestrator decisions 2026-11-20). Criteria 1 and 2 of the epic. orch lesson add records a scope (local or basicly) and, for a basicly-scope lesson, an origin. No consumer repository name is recorded; the reproduction command must stand alone. The refusal reuses the existing rules, one rule in one place: MACHINE_PATH_RULES and ABSOLUTE_PATH_RULE in .basicly/core/kit/tracker/redact.py, and identity_pattern() with the machine-username rule in .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py, including its configured-holder exemption (basicly-5v1rrl9). Host names stay uncovered, because no rule for them exists.
payload.title: Record a scope and an origin on each lesson and refuse a machine path or user name

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
WHEN orch lesson close names a repository checkout and a commit that is not on that checkout's default branch (git merge-base --is-ancestor), THE COMMAND SHALL refuse it by name and append no event.
WHEN the commit is on that default branch, THE COMMAND SHALL append one close event that records the repository and the full commit id.
WHEN orch lesson close gets free text instead of a commit, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse it by name.
A test in tests/ proves each case.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
WHEN orch lessons export gets a basicly checkout as its target, THE COMMAND SHALL write a patch that touches only basicly catalog source paths, plus a pull request body that holds the origin and evidence of each basicly-scope lesson.
WHEN the target is not a basicly checkout, THE COMMAND SHALL refuse it by name.
The export SHALL include only basicly-scope lessons.
A test runs the export in a consumer fixture with the network blocked.

payload.text: Orchestrator decision 2026-11-20: by default the export prints the gh pr create command and does not run it. A session in a workspace whose rules allow it may run the command (here the Orchestrator push rule, with the owner informed). A plain consumer keeps print-only. The acceptance must test both modes, and print-only must be the default.

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
When basicly finds a learning in a consumer repository, I want it to flow back to the main basicly repository with its evidence, so every installation improves the harness.

## Owner intent
2026-11-17, relayed by the Orchestrator in his words: "basicly must be able to learn and self-improve - if it is happening in a client repo, then it must know how to bring back the learning to the main basilcy repo, for example by creating a PR."

## Shape
Shaped with the Orchestrator on 2026-11-20. A consumer recognises a learning only from a recorded fact: a repeated hook or gate refusal (counted by orch errors), a person's correction, or a basicly command that fails or refuses wrongly. A lesson is basicly-scope only when its fix changes a file that basicly install writes; only those are exported. A lesson records no consumer repository name. It closes only by a commit on the default branch of the named checkout. Cuts: .1 shape (this), L1b scope and origin, .2 verified close, .3 orch errors in the kit, .4 export to basicly, .5 pull request.
